mu-af236cec.stem: What are the nerve supply and action of tibialis anterior?
options: Deep fibular nerve – everts the foot
Deep fibular nerve – dorsiflexes and inverts the foot
Superficial fibular nerve – everts the foot
mu-af236cec.explanation: Tibialis anterior is the strongest dorsiflexor in the anterior compartment of the leg and raises the medial border of the foot. The anterior compartment muscles are supplied by the deep fibular nerve.

mu-fea7541d.stem: Which nerve supplies fibularis longus and brevis?
mu-fea7541d.explanation: The lateral compartment muscles (fibularis longus and brevis) are supplied by the superficial fibular nerve and are the main evertors of the foot. The nerve then pierces the fascia and supplies most of the skin of the dorsum of the foot.

mu-9f569c87.stem: After a tight cast, a patient develops severe pain at the front of the leg; passive flexion of the big toe increases the pain, and sensation is lost in a small area between the 1st and 2nd toes. Which compartment and nerve are affected?
mu-9f569c87.explanation: In anterior compartment syndrome the muscles within (tibialis anterior, EHL, EDL) hurt on passive stretch. The nerve of this compartment is the deep fibular nerve, which supplies only the first web space in the skin. Early fasciotomy is needed.

mu-1fabd47c.stem: Which spinal segment does the ankle (Achilles) reflex mainly assess?
mu-1fabd47c.explanation: The ankle reflex tests segment S1 (S1–S2) through triceps surae and the tibial nerve. The patellar reflex assesses L4 (L3–L4). L5 has no reliable reflex.

mu-82c620d1.stem: Which muscle is called the 'peripheral heart' because of its contribution to venous return?
mu-82c620d1.explanation: Soleus contains large venous sinuses; when it contracts it squeezes the deep veins and pumps blood upwards (muscle pump). Prolonged immobility disables this pump and raises the risk of deep vein thrombosis.

mu-b7ee4b0d.stem: What is the order of structures behind the medial malleolus from front to back?
options: Flexor digitorum longus, tibialis posterior, tibial nerve, posterior tibial artery, flexor hallucis longus
Tibial nerve, posterior tibial artery, tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus
Tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial artery/vein, tibial nerve, flexor hallucis longus
Flexor hallucis longus, tibial nerve, posterior tibial artery, flexor digitorum longus, tibialis posterior
Tibialis posterior, posterior tibial artery, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus, tibial nerve
mu-b7ee4b0d.explanation: In the tarsal tunnel (under the flexor retinaculum) the order from front to back is: tibialis posterior, FDL, artery and veins, tibial nerve, FHL. Compression of the tibial nerve here is tarsal tunnel syndrome. The posterior tibial pulse is felt between the medial malleolus and the heel.

mu-8fe294a0.stem: A basketball player jumping feels as if kicked in the back of the heel; lying prone, squeezing the calf does not plantarflex the foot (positive Thompson test). Which structure is injured?
mu-8fe294a0.explanation: The Achilles tendon is the common tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus. In a complete rupture squeezing the calf does not move the foot. The slender plantaris tendon may remain intact but cannot produce the movement on its own.

mu-ccb4be63.stem: Which leg muscle, absent in some people, has a tendon that can be used as a tendon graft?
mu-ccb4be63.explanation: Plantaris has a small belly and one of the longest tendons in the body; it descends between gastrocnemius and soleus to attach to the calcaneus. Because it has little functional importance, it can be harvested as a graft.

mu-acbb7f78.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscles of the dorsum of the foot (extensor digitorum brevis and extensor hallucis brevis)?
mu-acbb7f78.explanation: The short extensors, the only muscle group on the dorsum of the foot, are supplied by the lateral branch of the deep fibular nerve. All the muscles of the sole come from the medial and lateral plantar branches of the tibial nerve.

mu-52844253.stem: Which of the following plantar muscles is supplied by the medial plantar nerve?
mu-52844253.explanation: The medial plantar nerve resembles the median nerve in the hand: it supplies abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis and the 1st lumbrical. All the other plantar muscles are supplied by the lateral plantar nerve (the counterpart of the ulnar nerve in the hand).

mu-6e025948.stem: Which muscle, supplied by the trochlear nerve, turns the eyeball down and out?
mu-6e025948.explanation: The superior oblique tendon passes through the trochlea, changes direction and attaches to the posterior superolateral quadrant of the eyeball; it intorts the eye and turns it down and out. The trochlear nerve (IV) supplies only this muscle. In clinical testing, looking down with the eye adducted assesses this muscle.
notes: It turns the eye up and in; supplied by the oculomotor nerve.
It turns the eye down and in; supplied by the oculomotor nerve.
It only abducts; supplied by the abducens nerve.
It turns the eye up and out; supplied by the oculomotor nerve.

mu-6c8964ef.stem: Which muscle produces upward gaze when the eye is looking inwards (adducted)?
mu-6c8964ef.explanation: In clinical examination the obliques are tested with the eye adducted and the recti with it abducted: looking up while looking in tests inferior oblique, looking up while looking out tests superior rectus. Inferior oblique is supplied by the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve.
notes: It is the muscle of upward gaze when looking out.
It raises the eyelid; it does not move the eyeball.
It is the muscle of downward gaze when looking in.

mu-27152caf.stem: A patient presenting with an aneurysm has complete drooping of the right eyelid; when the lid is lifted the right eye looks down and out and the pupil is dilated and unreactive to light. Which nerve is affected?
mu-27152caf.explanation: In oculomotor palsy levator palpebrae (complete ptosis), superior, inferior and medial recti and inferior oblique are paralysed; the eye turns down and out under the unopposed lateral rectus (VI) and superior oblique (IV). The parasympathetic fibres on the surface of the nerve are affected early by compression, so the pupil dilates. A posterior communicating artery aneurysm is the classic cause.
notes: In Horner syndrome the ptosis is mild and the pupil is small.
When paralysed the eye turns in; there is no ptosis.
It closes the eye; it does not raise the lid.
When paralysed the eye cannot look down in adduction; there is no ptosis.

mu-b7191b04.stem: Which of the following extra-ocular muscles does NOT arise from the common tendinous ring?
mu-b7191b04.explanation: The four recti arise from the common tendinous ring surrounding the optic canal and the medial part of the superior orbital fissure. Inferior oblique arises from the anteromedial floor of the orbit (orbital surface of the maxilla) and is the only extra-ocular muscle that does not originate at the back of the orbit.
